title: Scallion Crisp Mongolian Flank Tray
seoTitle: Scallion Crisp Mongolian Flank Tray | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Mongolian beef on the flat-top—crisp flank, glossy sauce, rice for ten
subtitle: Crisp flank strips, sweet-savory sauce, and scallions for ten
description: Flank steak strips coat in cornstarch, sear crisp on the griddle, and toss with sweet-savory Mongolian sauce and scallions. Served over steamed rice.

steps.title: Slice and coat flank
steps.instruction: Slice flank thin against the grain. Toss with cornstarch until lightly coated. Shake off excess. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use coconut aminos, Chinese black vinegar, dried Thai chilies, shaoxing wine as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Use peanut oil as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Build Mongolian sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk soy, brown sugar, hoisin, garlic, and ginger until smooth. Hold warm at 140°F. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 450°F. Add oil in thin film. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear beef batches
steps.instruction: Sear flank strips in single layers 2 minutes per side until crisp and 130°F. Work in batches. Hold at 170°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Griddle scallions
steps.instruction: Quickly griddle green onion pieces 1–2 minutes until lightly charred. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sauce toss at service
steps.instruction: Toss crisp beef with warm Mongolian sauce and scallions at the line—not during long hold. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Hold sauced beef
steps.instruction: If needed, hold sauced beef covered at 170°F up to 15 minutes max. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Serve Mongolian beef over steamed rice. About 8 oz beef per firefighter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Cornstarch coat is the crisp secret—don't skip or oversaturate.
Single-layer searing only; crowded beef steams and greys.
Sauce toss at service keeps crust from going soggy in hold.
tonightSpread: Mongolian beef flat top with steamed rice.
Quick cucumber salad with rice vinegar.
leftovers: Mongolian beef lettuce wraps next shift.
Chop into fried rice with extra scallions.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Mongolian beef is a flat-top classic that isn't stir-fry night in a wok. Cornstarch crust survives hold at 170°F better than naked beef strips.
mealPrepNotes: Slice flank thin against grain. Sear in batches at 450°F—do not crowd. Sauce toss at service. Hold beef covered at 170°F up to 25 minutes.
